enhanced.fullText:
The EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP), established under the Clean Air Act and codified at 40 CFR Part 98, mandates comprehensive annual reporting of greenhouse gas emissions from large-scale stationary sources, including higher education institutions operating qualifying facilities. This federal regulation, effective since 2010, requires universities with facilities that emit 25,000 metric tons CO2 equivalent (CO2e) or more annually to submit detailed emissions data to the Environmental Protection Agency.

The regulation's legal authority derives from the Clean Air Act Section 114, codified at 42 U.S.C. § 7414, which grants EPA broad investigatory and monitoring powers. Universities must report emissions of seven primary greenhouse gases: carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), perfluorocarbons (PFCs), sulfur hexafluoride (SF6), and nitrogen trifluoride (NF3), as specified in 40 CFR § 98.2.

Applicability to higher education institutions typically involves large campus operations including central energy plants, research facilities with significant fuel combustion, or specialized equipment exceeding threshold levels. Universities operating combined heat and power systems, research reactors, or extensive laboratory facilities with high energy consumption commonly trigger reporting requirements under 40 CFR § 98.2(a).

Key provisions require facilities to develop comprehensive monitoring plans, maintain detailed records, and submit annual GHG reports by March 31 following each calendar year, as mandated by 40 CFR § 98.3(c). Universities must register facilities in EPA's electronic GHG Reporting Tool (e-GGRT) and designate authorized representatives responsible for certifying report accuracy under penalty of perjury.

Enforcement mechanisms include civil penalties up to $48,864 per day per violation under 42 U.S.C. § 7413(d)(1), adjusted annually for inflation. EPA may assess penalties for failure to report, late submissions, incomplete data, or certification violations. The Agency conducts periodic audits and has authority to inspect facilities and records under 40 CFR § 98.7.

Recent amendments include expanded monitoring requirements for certain source categories and updated global warming potentials published in 40 CFR § 98.3(c)(5)(i). Universities must stay current with annual updates to avoid compliance violations and maintain accurate emissions calculations using EPA-approved methodologies.
enhanced.summary: Federal regulation requiring universities with facilities emitting 25,000+ metric tons CO2 equivalent annually to report greenhouse gas emissions to EPA by March 31 each year under Clean Air Act authority.
enhanced.requirements:
## Annual Reporting Obligations
- Submit comprehensive GHG emissions data by March 31 following each calendar year per 40 CFR § 98.3(c)
- Register qualifying facilities in EPA's electronic GHG Reporting Tool (e-GGRT)
- Designate authorized representatives to certify report accuracy under oath

## Monitoring and Documentation
- Develop facility-specific monitoring plans compliant with 40 CFR Part 98 methodologies
- Maintain detailed records of fuel consumption, emissions factors, and calculation procedures
- Implement quality assurance protocols for data collection and verification

## Compliance Management
- Conduct annual threshold determinations to assess continued applicability
- Update registration information and facility contacts within prescribed timeframes
- Coordinate with environmental health and safety personnel and facilities management

## Record Retention
- Preserve all supporting documentation for minimum three years per 40 CFR § 98.3(g)
- Maintain electronic copies of submitted reports and EPA correspondence
enhanced.reportingRequirements: Annual GHG emissions reports due March 31 each year via EPA's e-GGRT system. Initial facility registration required before first report submission. Immediate notification required for facility changes affecting applicability status per 40 CFR § 98.3.
